problem:
The system of equations

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}z-7x-5=0 \\ 4y-x-3z-2=0 \\ 2y+x-8=-2\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

 

can be represented using matrix notation as

$$
[\begin{aligned}-7 & 0 & 1 \\ -1 & 4 & a \\ b & 2 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 2 \\ c\end{aligned}].
$$

What are the values of $a,b,$ and $c?$

activity_context.topic_title: Representing 3x3 Systems of Equations Using a Matrix Product

feedback.problem:
The system of equations

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}-2x+y+z=-1 \\ z+3x-2y=3 \\ -y+2z-x=-4\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

can be represented using matrix notation as

$$
[\begin{aligned}-2 & 1 & 1 \\ 3 & b & 1 \\ -1 & -1 & c\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}a \\ 3 \\ -4\end{aligned}].
$$

What are the values of $a,b$ and $c?$
feedback.worked_solution:
First, let's write the system so that $x$, $y$, and $z$ appear in each equation in the correct order and all constants are on the right-hand side of the system:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}-2x+y+z=-1 \\ 3x-2y+z=3 \\ -x-y+2z=-4\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can write the system in the form $Ax=b,$ where

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}-2 & 1 & 1 \\ 3 & -2 & 1 \\ -1 & -1 & 2\end{aligned}]
$$

is the coefficient matrix,

$$
b=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 3 \\ -4\end{aligned}]
$$

is the column vector of constants, and

$$
x=[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]
$$

is the column vector of variables.

So, the equation $Ax=b$ becomes

$$
[\begin{aligned}-2 & 1 & 1 \\ 3 & -2 & 1 \\ -1 & -1 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 3 \\ -4\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, $a=-1,\,b=-2,\,c=2.$
